quest.title: Expectations Not to Be Betrayed
quest.description: You return with Yoimiya to Naganohara Fireworks, but discover a stowaway hiding inside the shop named Sakujirou. To prevent his capture at the hands of the Tenryou Commission, you must find a way for him to leave Inazuma while preparing for a fireworks show.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

talks.objective: Prepare a boat for Sakujirou alongside Yoimiya

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Kouichi! I'm here, how is the boat coming along?

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's... alright, I guess. Um, I was questioned though...

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: Wait, wait. Should we really be talking about this in front of them?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, don't worry, they're my friends, you can trust them! They came with me to check up on the boat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! You could say we're all in the same BOAT here! Haha...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Pleasure to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: Oh, I see... Sorry, I didn't mean to doubt you, I'm just being cautious. The boat is ready, but I'll have to be discreet moving it here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why is that?

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: Because of the Sakoku Decree. The Tenryou Commission is really suspicious of any kind of seaborne vessel. Even the smallest ones — they'll stop and interrogate us, demanding to know what we plan on doing with it. It's a real nuisance.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I understand. I'm sorry for dragging you into this mess...

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: Haha, don't be silly. I'm actually happy that you came to me for help. I've always come to you for fireworks, and again this time — so just consider this my way of saying thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: Right, I'll go fetch the boat now. I should be back shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Thank you! If it's on the way, you can always pick up your fireworks from my house. Everything was made in strict accordance with what was on the paper slip, you won't find the slightest thing wrong with them.

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: Alright then. The fireworks show will be starting soon, won't it — you should make sure your new friends get to see it. It's an Inazuman tradition, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Yep, that's the plan! ...Oh! You know what, you should tell them about your past — about the first time you ordered fireworks from my family.

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: That's a long story, actually... Where do I start...

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: ...Oh, uh — maybe I'll come back to that after moving the boat here.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, right, yeah. Got caught up in the conversation there, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: Okay, well, I'll leave you to it for now and meet you back here later.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hehe, lucky he reminded me, otherwise I would've ended up chatting the rest of the day away.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I've been so busy with the fireworks business these past few days that I haven't had a moment to stop and chat with anyone. Ugh, it's killing me.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Of course, Pops is happy to listen to me chatter away... but because he can hardly hear anything, it's difficult to get an interesting reaction from him...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: ...Aaaand I'm doing it again, aren't I? Ugh. What I meant to say was, while Kouichi is bringing the boat here, we should try to find some firework materials.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I need to make fireworks not just for you guys, but for those kids and Sakujirou as well. We're missing a lot of materials.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If it's too much trouble, don't worry about us.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: It'll be fine. It's actually like this every year, there's always a bunch of extra orders to slot in here and there.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: When people want fireworks, it's always because they have something to commemorate. And if they miss the chance, they might never get another one. So, no matter how busy I am, I'm always happy to take their orders.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what you're trying to say is that you enjoy the work?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, I do! I really do. Being born into a family of fireworks makers, I feel like since I was a kid, I've been obsessed with watching things go BOOM and then seeing all the lights and colors and...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: ...Uh, but what I really wanted to say was: Don't worry about me, it'll all be fine!

choices.text: Oh, so THAT's what you meant...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Sorry, sorry! It's just that good conversation can be as fleeting as fireworks, sometimes, you know? So when I'm in the mood and I've got a lot to say, I just have to get it all out there in one go and leave no regrets!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Let's head to the city, I think I'll try my luck with some people that I know.

choices.text: Your main point got a bit buried in all the extra information.

talks.objective: Look for firework materials in the city

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Ah, just as I thought, he isn't back yet. But not to worry, because actually, I've been hoping for a chance to have a nice long chat with you all day.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Sorry for dragging you with me everywhere... Everyone's been so good to me though. It's all gone really smoothly, hee-hee.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* Feels like Paimon has barely spoken a word this whole trip.

choices.text: You seem to get along well with everyone.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I felt like I was neglecting you guys, so I wanted to find an opportunity to catch up.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: When we first met, I was in a hurry. We didn't have a chance to sit down and have a proper chat.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: You guys are travelers, right? So, where else did you go before coming to Inazuma?

choices.text: Mondstadt, the City of Freedom.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Sounds great! I heard that they pretty much have no rules over there, right? So people are free to live their life however they want, doing whatever makes them happy.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: My pops actually received a gift from one of his old customers over there. It was from the winery or something...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Dawn Winery! Their Dandelion Wine is super famous.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Oh, yes! That's the one. I remember when he drank it — hee-hee, I've never seen him enjoy a bottle of wine so much in his life! He was telling me all night about how good it tasted.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: My friend once said to me that only people with a strong will and a clear purpose decide to go traveling. Maybe it's to see a certain view or to fulfill a certain wish...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: So. What made you guys embark on your treacherous journey to Inazuma?

choices.text: To track down an enemy god.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And to find a lost family member, too.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: You were separated from your family because of a god?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: That must be really tough.

choices.text: Sometimes it is.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I get it. Well, if that's how it is, then that's how it is. Eh-he, y'know, I was going to ask you guys if you wanted to stay here in Inazuma.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Unlike the outside world, what Inazuma seeks is eternity. In other words, a state of tranquility, where very little ever changes.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: The advantage of that is that if you're tired from your journey, Inazuma's a great place to come and rest.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Umm... let me put it this way. I was just worried that you might be getting weary, and if you keep pressing on in that state, you might start to lose sight of the things that made you want to start your journey in the first place.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Sometimes, that's also just how it is.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: When you're exhausted, everything becomes an uphill struggle. Even trying to have fun — you won't be able to enjoy yourself if you're too tired.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: An adventurer friend of mine once told me that if you're too focused on reaching the end of the race, you'll miss a lot of opportunities and precious moments to be had along the way.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Don't worry though, I'm sure I can think of some way to get you feeling relaxed and happy!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: And you're here now, so even if you're gonna leave eventually, I wanna make sure you at least leave with fond memories.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Who knows — once you're reunited with your family, maybe you'll find Inazuma the right kind of place to call home.

choices.text: I'll add it to my list of candidates.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Hehe, I already have an idea of the color and type of fireworks I wanna give you guys. I'll keep it a secret for now, though.

response.speaker: Kouichi
response.text: Yoimiya, I'm back! Sorry to keep you waiting! Let's head over to the boat... or, uh, did you want to keep chatting a little longer?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We just finished, as it happens.

response.speaker: Kouichi
response.text: Okay, good. Let's go, then. Just act naturally, though, we don't want to raise any suspicion.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If it can withstand the storms out on the ocean, it must be super sturdy, right?

response.speaker: Kouichi
response.text: Absolutely. Rest assured that the quality is guaranteed.

choices.text: #It also depends what my {F#brother}{M#sister} thinks.
I'll bear that in mind.
I'm slowly learning to cope.
#I'm looking for my lost {F#brother}{M#sister}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And we're looking for answers from the gods, too.

choices.text: Liyue, the nation of contracts.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I haven't been to Liyue before, but from what I've heard from Miss Beidou, it sounds like a really interesting place.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: But something big happened there recently, right? Didn't their archon leave all of a sudden?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, a lot of crazy things went down as a result.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Luckily, everyone worked together to stave off a huge disaster that could have wiped out the whole city.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Oh, well that's good to hear. I gotta say, it's pretty remarkable that the citizens managed to step up and keep things going even after their archon left.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I mean, I sure can't imagine Inazuma without the Shogun.

choices.text: It was nice just listening quietly.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hello, Morihiko. How's business these days?

dialogues.speaker: Morihiko
dialogues.text: Haha, Yoimiya, there you are. I thought you might show up.

dialogues.speaker: Morihiko
dialogues.text: No need to beat about the bush — you'll be here for the firework materials, I assume? I put a batch aside just for you. It'll definitely be enough.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Huh? Really? How did you know!?

dialogues.speaker: Morihiko
dialogues.text: Because a fireworks show is coming up! And that usually means you'll be running all over the place trying to get your hands on some last-minute materials.

dialogues.speaker: Morihiko
dialogues.text: I've come to expect it now. There's always a few extras unaccounted for, eh.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: So sorry for bothering you every time...

dialogues.speaker: Morihiko
dialogues.text: Ah, come on now, you know I didn't mean it like that! I'd sooner have my business go under than turn down one of your requests.

dialogues.speaker: Morihiko
dialogues.text: What about you two, are you the ones needing some fireworks made?

choices.text: Hi, yes, thank you ever so much.

response.speaker: Morihiko
response.text: Haha, it's no trouble at all, my friend.

response.speaker: Morihiko
response.text: Once when I'd had an argument with my son, Yoimiya was the one who came and calmed him down.

response.speaker: Morihiko
response.text: I'm hopeless at communicating with him. If it wasn't for Yoimiya, who knows, he probably would've run away by now...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Naw, it was never gonna come to that. He's a sensitive kid and he cares a lot about your feelings. It's just... he doesn't know how to express it.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Maybe if you turned that frown upside down once in a while, he might feel more at ease.

response.speaker: Morihiko
response.text: Yeah, I guess I'm probably too serious around him...

response.speaker: Morihiko
response.text: Which is strange, because I don't think I'm anything like that when I'm talking with other people...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Don't worry about it! No one's perfect. If you have any more trouble in the future, just come to me.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Even if it's not fireworks-related, I'll happily oblige. Customers come first, always.

response.speaker: Morihiko
response.text: Haha, alright then. Everyone's always saying what a good kid you are. Your father must be very proud of you.

response.speaker: Morihiko
response.text: Go ahead and take the ore, by the way. It's on the house.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Oh no you don't! That's out of the question!

response.speaker: Morihiko
response.text: Don't worry, just take it as a token of my gratitude.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Gratitude won't pay your bills, though... Don't do this to me, can't we just play by normal business rules here?

response.speaker: Morihiko
response.text: I already said it's fine. Please, just take it. Surely you've got a whole load of other things you need to get done today?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Um... Well, how about this, then: I'll record this in my notebook, and we can consider it a down payment against any fireworks you want to purchase in the future.

response.speaker: Morihiko
response.text: *sigh* There's no convincing you, is there...

response.speaker: Morihiko
response.text: Alright then, if you insist.

response.speaker: Morihiko
response.text: Pass on my regards to your dad. Tell him Morihiko wishes him health and happiness.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Will do. You look after yourself as well. Don't push yourself too hard — you don't wanna make yourself ill again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Everyone seems to really like you, Yoimiya.

choices.text: Seems like you'd happily do anything for anyone.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: You're not the first person to say that. In fact, some people think I'll literally do any favor they ask me to.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: When that happens, I say to them "Hey! This is a fireworks store! We do fireworks!"

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: But, ugh. They don't always listen. So, it can't be helped... but also, it's not really a big deal.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Anyway, we've got all the materials we need now, so that solves that problem!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Next, we just need to go find someone to process them!

choices.text: Fireworks are pretty important to Inazumans, huh?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Well, for one thing, if you want to commemorate something, naturally you're gonna want something loud, bright, and beautiful.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: But I think more importantly than that, everyone trusts us. If it wasn't for our customers, we wouldn't be able to stay in business.

choices.text: Sorry for the trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hajime, Mr. Amenoma! It's me!

dialogues.speaker: Hajime
dialogues.text: Ah, Yoimiya. If I'm not mistaken, you must be here for some firework materials?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like everyone knows how busy Yoimiya gets leading up to the fireworks show.

dialogues.speaker: Hajime
dialogues.text: I'm very sorry, would you be able to wait for a while? I have quite a backlog of weapons orders right now.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: No worri— Oh wait, actually... Ahh, yeah, that could be a problem... some worries.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, how about this! Do you need a hand? As long as we can get through your orders, you can help me process my ore, right?

dialogues.speaker: Hajime
dialogues.text: Uh... that will depend on my master...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, you don't mind, do you, Mr. Amenoma! As you know, it's not long now until the Naganohara Fireworks Show starts.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: There's still a lot of fireworks left to make. If I don't finish them on time...

dialogues.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
dialogues.text: Talkative as ever, I see, dear child.

dialogues.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
dialogues.text: The essence of Amenoma Art is patience and focus. When the mind is disturbed, it will show in the blade that is forged.

dialogues.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
dialogues.text: If you badger Hajime like this, you will only succeed in disrupting his concentration.

dialogues.speaker: Hajime
dialogues.text: B—But, this is a special circumstance, surely! The Naganohara Fireworks Show is right around the corner...

dialogues.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
dialogues.text: So give me your ore, and I will process it for you.

dialogues.speaker: Hajime
dialogues.text: Huh!? Master... you mean, you'll do the work personally?

dialogues.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
dialogues.text: Is that so surprising? It is, after all, the only option.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Thank you for helping out, Mr. Amenoma!

dialogues.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
dialogues.text: You're quite welcome. The Naganohara Fireworks Show is an important event, this I know well. In addition to this, I am indebted to Ryuunosuke for all the business he has given me.

dialogues.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
dialogues.text: But Yoimiya... you should plan things more carefully in the future. Do not rush everything at the last minute.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hehe, I'll try my best. In the future, I'll get some extra materials in to cover any unexpected changes of plan late in the day.

dialogues.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
dialogues.text: *sigh* Though for you, dear child, no matter how much you prepare in advance, it may never be enough...

dialogues.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
dialogues.text: Excuse me. I will be back shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Wow, Mr. Amenoma! Just look at the shape and size of these grains... It's beautiful. I'm at a loss for words.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: It's been a while since I've seen you take up your tools, but it looks like your craft hasn't degraded one bit.

dialogues.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
dialogues.text: Of course. I have studied these techniques my whole life... they are impossible for me to forget.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So have Amenoma Art and Naganohara Fireworks been working together for a really long time already?

dialogues.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
dialogues.text: Back in the day, it was my master and Ryuunosuke's father. The people may have changed from one generation to another, but the ingredients required to make fireworks have remained the same.

dialogues.speaker: Amenoma Tougo
dialogues.text: Hajime, in the future, this will be up to you.

dialogues.speaker: Hajime
dialogues.text: I know, I know...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hahaha, alright, I won't bother you guys any longer. Remember to come and watch the fireworks!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: #Okay, {NICKNAME}, time to head off.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Kouichi probably isn't back just yet, but let's go wait for him.

talks.objective: Head to the designated location to meet Kouichi
Go and confirm the ship's condition

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's way too small!

choices.text: It is technically sturdy though...

response.speaker: Kouichi
response.text: Can't be helped, I'm afraid, this is the biggest and sturdiest boat that I can provide. It's built from the finest Inazuman timber.

response.speaker: Kouichi
response.text: Still, I'll be the first to admit that if he's planning to ride this into the storm, it's going to be exceedingly dangerous...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I'm also hoping Sakujirou won't have to use it. It's just there as a last resort.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I gotta say, though, Kouichi, it feels like your craft has improved once again.

response.speaker: Kouichi
response.text: Haha, I'm not the one you should be praising. It's all thanks to the guys who kindly pitched in.

response.speaker: Kouichi
response.text: To avoid detection, we each worked on our own materials separately, then assembled them secretly in the night.

response.speaker: Kouichi
response.text: This is the largest we could afford to build it. Any bigger and there's no way it would pass the Tenryou Commission's inspection.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Let's store the boat here for now, then. I'll fill Sakujirou in when I get back, he'll need to make some preparations before setting sail.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-oh, Paimon feels really worried all of a sudden... Uh... Doesn't helping Sakujirou make you a collaborator in the eyes of the Tenryou Commission?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Haha, maybe it does, but I knew what I was getting into from the moment I agreed to help him.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: My family has pretty good connections with the Yashiro Commission. We work very closely with them. And whenever there's a national event of any sort, the other two Commissions come to us, too.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: As long as I'm polite and respectful and don't cause a fuss, they won't look to cause trouble for me, either.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: And anyway, to your point about collaboration... you've been helping out too, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true, this was all a collaborative effort... wait, huh? *gasp* Oh no!

choices.text: We were chased by the Millelith in Liyue, too.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Ah, so you're seasoned crooks already, eh? Don't know what I was worried about then! Hehe.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Anyway, thanks for everything, Kouichi.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Oh, and your fireworks are ready, so just go and pick them up from my house whenever you want. While you're there, you can get my pops to settle the boat construction fees.

response.speaker: Kouichi
response.text: Oh, don't worry about paying anything. Third Sis would be sure to scold me if she found out I'd taken Mora from the Naganoharas.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who's Third Sis?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Oh! Uh, let me explain this one, it's a story my pops told me. There used to be a thriving merchants' guild in Inazuma, it got really prosperous.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: At one point, there were a dozen or so kids born around the same time to the families of the guild. They all grew up together, each of them learning their respective family's business.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: They were a tightly knit group of friends, but eventually, they all grew up and decided they each wanted to go into business themselves.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: It was inevitable that their business would send them all to different corners of the world, and that they'd have far less opportunity to see each other in the future.

response.speaker: Kouichi
response.text: That's right. Just before we went our separate ways, the eldest of the group suggested that we should all go watch some fireworks together one last time.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Hehe, they were all very ambitious types, and each had their own knack for doing business. One by one, they left, until Kouichi was the only one of them remaining in Inazuma.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: After that, he hardly saw them. But whenever one of them did come back to visit, fireworks would always be involved.

response.speaker: Kouichi
response.text: Yeah, no matter how close you and your friends are, there's always going to be some distance after being separated for a long time. But as soon as the fireworks lit up the sky, it'd instantly take us right back to our childhood, and we'd be chatting away like in the old days.

response.speaker: Kouichi
response.text: To us, those memories are eternal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh, so this is what you meant when you were talking about commemorating things.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Yep, that's exactly right. That's why I can't let people down when they're counting on me for their fireworks.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Anyway, I need to go update Sakujirou. See you, Kouichi! Thanks again for your help!

response.speaker: Kouichi
response.text: Yeah, I should get out of here, too. I don't want to get caught red-handed.

choices.text: Do we have to be the bad guys in Inazuma as well?
Makes me think of Atsuko.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: The boat is a-ready and waiting. I'll mark the location for you on the map. Before you leave, I recommend that you pack some food and water. You can never be too prepared.

dialogues.speaker: Sakujirou
dialogues.text: Ah...

dialogues.speaker: Sakujirou
dialogues.text: *sigh* After how much effort it took to get back in, it's hard to convince myself to leave again... especially when I'll be going up against the stormy ocean on a tiny little boat... My prospects don't look great.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Well, they won't look much better if you get caught by the Tenryou Commission...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I'm afraid that sooner or later, they are going to find you here. Time is starting to run out.

dialogues.speaker: Sakujirou
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, I'll make sure to get out of here before they come. I promise I won't cause you and your family any more trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I didn't mean it like that. If we ever ran into any problems, I'm sure I'd figure something out.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: But if the Tenryou Commission does catch up to you, then make a run for the boat.

dialogues.speaker: Sakujirou
dialogues.text: Okay. I won't let them catch me...

dialogues.speaker: Sakujirou
dialogues.text: But... *sigh* Ah, I guess this whole trip was a waste in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why did you wanna come back to Inazuma anyway? Is there something you wanted to do?

dialogues.speaker: Sakujirou
dialogues.text: I didn't use to like this place at all, that's why I left. But looking back on things now, I was really just running away from my responsibilities.

dialogues.speaker: Sakujirou
dialogues.text: Once I started to realize that, I got restless. I couldn't stop thinking about the people and the things I'd left behind...

dialogues.speaker: Sakujirou
dialogues.text: So, I... Ah, forget it, what does it matter now. It's too late, anyway. I originally wanted to make up for all my regrets, but instead, I found myself in the situation I'm in now.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: *sigh* What a pity...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Talk to us about it, maybe we could—

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: If only there was no Sakoku Decree, huh.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Anyway, don't worry, we're not going to bother you about it. We'll keep trying to buy you as much time as possible until you reach your final decision.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: The Tenryou Commission... If only they weren't so overzealous, there might be a way...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, that's right! That elderly couple, old customers of ours — their son's in the Tenryou Commission, isn't he? Yeah, quite high up, as well.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: That's it! I'll go talk to them. Maybe they can do something!

dialogues.speaker: Sakujirou
dialogues.text: Um... Are you sure they won't just report me instead?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, don't worry about that. They're really nice people, I know them well. They won't cause us any issues.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Alright, you should get back indoors, Sakujirou. We'll be back in no time at all.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Okay, let's go. Time waits for no one.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Wait, hang on... What about the fireworks? All those materials... there's so many orders to finish...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: ...Pops! Pops!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, never mind. I know, I'll write him a note telling him to sort out the fireworks!

dialogues.speaker: Sakujirou
dialogues.text: Thank you for helping me with the escape plan.

dialogues.speaker: Sakujirou
dialogues.text: I wish I wasn't so indecisive...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Question! Doesn't it hurt your voice, talking all the time?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: It can get uncomfortable, I guess... But what else would I be using my voice for?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... you kinda have a point.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Ah, here we are!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Okay, story time. So, whenever Kouichi brings one of his friends from the trade association to see me, they always mention how they used to play with me when I was a kid, or held me once as a baby, or something.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: But there are so many of them in that friendship group, and I don't remember anything from that age anyway. So I never have a clue who they are.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: One time, he shows up with another one of his friends, and the friend asks me if I remember him.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: So I'm like, "Yes, I do! You held me once when I was just a baby!"

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Kouichi just bursts out laughing and says actually, this is one of his carpenter friends. Turns out he's a lot younger than he looks — just a few years older than me.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I went bright red and must have apologized, like, a million times. Arghhhh, it was so embarrassing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahem, why did you cut Paimon off earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Because what he needs isn't an answer, just time.

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Hehe, she's always full of life.

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: That's my girl, that's my girl...
